consigna: One sustained spoken production of at least twelve minutes: present a case to two audiences in the same session — a technical one and a lay one — steering the discussion, predicting outcomes and steering the listener's sympathy without stating an opinion. With a person or recorded alone.
requisitos: A scenario tree with a wildcard and the signal that distinguishes the paths (week 26)
A consistent thread of charged wording, with no explicit evaluation (week 27)
Feedback offered as a hypothesis, framed differently from the last review (week 28)
One unannounced redirection and one repair between two speakers (week 30)
Register handled on at least four axes across the two audiences (week 31)
Compression calibrated to the audience: an absolute construction for the technical part, verbs kept for the lay part (weeks 32 and 33)
microtareas: *Mon (10 min).* Reread the corrections from weeks 26 to 33 and note the recurring one.
*Wed (5 min).* Write three sentences carrying charged wording, an absolute construction and a graded prediction together.
*Fri (10 min).* Record the twelve minutes. Then check: did the lay half stay compressed like the technical half?
autochequeo: Did the charged wording do the arguing, or did I state an opinion after all?
Was the redirection unannounced and still effective?
Did the compression fit each audience?
promptCorreccion: This is a review of six skills at once: scenario prediction, connotation as argument, feedback as hypothesis, conversational steering, multi-axis register and audience-calibrated compression. (1) For each, say whether it is present and whether it is done well. (2) Say which collapsed. (3) Give me one sentence carrying three of them. Correct nothing outside these six areas. ---
